clue.text: A number of enmities for a faithful friend

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
hates, as a noun, are things one hates: enmities

explanation.surface: Someone with plenty of grudges is held up, oddly, as a model of loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Achates is the companion of Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid, whose loyalty made his name a byword for a faithful friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Aeneid this character is the hero's ever-loyal companion, so his name stands for any devoted comrade.

clue.text: Skill is all round the street, say the painters

parts.note: art is skill

indicators.note: all round says the word is goes around the next piece

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Painters are everywhere along the street, showing their talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters are one kind of artist.

clue.text: The Queen goes in a strange launch around the East, and it is immensely arduous

indicators.note: goes in puts the monarch's letters inside the rest
around has the shuffled letters wrap the compass point
strange says the letters of launch are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch boards an odd boat that circles east, a gruelling trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' shuffles the boat word, 'around' wraps that round E, and the monarch 'goes in'. Hercules was the strongman of Greek myth whose twelve labours were famously hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks fit for Hercules, the strongman of myth, are enormously demanding.

clue.text: Gratitude over disapproval for what is forbidden

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
a boo expresses disapproval

explanation.surface: Thanks give way to jeers over something banned.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' simply puts TA above BOO. TA is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a social prohibition, something not permitted.

clue.text: Feels pain when saints hold a vehicle up

indicators.note: hold puts the reversed vehicle between the two letters for saints

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint, so two saints give SS

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Holy people hurt as they lift a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to sting or hurt.

clue.text: Austere person has to quote a number with union backing

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the whole string of pieces from right to left

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
SA stands for the Union of South Africa, the country's name before 1961

explanation.surface: A stern figure must name a figure with the support of a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union, but it is the old Union of South Africa, SA. 'backing' turns CITE + C + SA, giving the letters in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic is someone who practises severe self-denial, the very picture of an austere person.

clue.text: Scientist who is an atrocious person, cutting up mice

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

indicators.note: up, as in stirred up, says the letters of mice are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heartless researcher dissects laboratory mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' is part of the surface picture of dissection; 'up' rearranges MICE into EMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic is a scholar at a university, here taken as a scientist.

clue.text: Soldier who holds the East to be not spiritual

indicators.note: holds says the soldier's rank goes round the compass letter

parts.note: a corporal is a soldier
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A soldier posted to the Orient is decidedly worldly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily, of the material world rather than the spirit.

clue.text: A hundred is found in the fastening

indicators.note: is found in places the first pieces within the word the

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred pounds turns up inside a clasp.
explanation.walkthrough: A tache is an old word for a clasp or buckle.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic noun means a clasp or buckle used to fasten things.

clue.text: Trench which is ingenious when holding the catcher

indicators.note: when holding says the clever word contains the catcher

parts.note: cute can mean clever or ingenious
a net is a catcher

explanation.surface: A ditch is a clever device for trapping things.
explanation.walkthrough: A cunette is a small channel cut along the bottom of a dry moat.
explanation.definitionFit: In fortification this is a narrow ditch dug in the floor of a larger one.

clue.text: Give headgear back to artist to make something boring

indicators.note: give back means the hat word is turned round, read from end to start

parts.note: a beret is a piece of headgear
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: Return a hat to the painter who lent it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling: a terebra is a boring organ, such as an insect's ovipositor.
explanation.definitionFit: In zoology this is a drilling or piercing organ, so literally a thing that bores holes.

clue.text: One who may be fair is able to become mainly dark-skinned

indicators.note: the word fair is to become something else, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: A fair-skinned person turns out able to change into a dark-skinned one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' shuffles the letters of 'fair' into AFRI. 'One who may be' is padding: the clue plays fair against dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes people of the continent whose population is, for the most part, of dark complexion.

clue.text: Failing to consider currently popular London club member

parts.note: a Spur is a player or fan of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club known as Spurs
something of the moment is in fashion right now

explanation.surface: A trendy footballer from a London club is praised for being in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur is a north London football club nicknamed Spurs. The phrase means done on impulse, without thought.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulsive decision is made without pausing to think it over, as when someone acts without due consideration.

clue.text: Range in which I go astray in the country

indicators.note: in which marks the country as the place that holds the wandering speaker

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
to err is to go astray

explanation.surface: A hiker admits to losing the way among the mountains out in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like countryside, but it is a particular country, South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged mountain range, as in the Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: Parliamentarian who has a lot of drinks with froth on

indicators.note: on in a down clue says the froth goes on top of, so after, the drinks

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
the head is the froth on beer

explanation.surface: An MP is buying beers topped with foam.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were Parliament's supporters in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the Parliament side's soldiers and supporters in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Drink left outside for the dog

parts.note: washing left outside on the line is aired
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A drink is put out in the garden for the pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large breed of terrier, named after a Yorkshire valley.

clue.text: Rare visit reorganised by someone new to the scene

indicators.note: reorganised says the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An infrequent visit is rearranged by a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is an upstart who has recently arrived in society.

clue.text: Close observers detect a woman among lots of fellows

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Close observers detect a woman among lots of fellows' (8): SCAN or ANN(E) is visible but no reading of 'lots of fellows' supplies the remaining letters of SCANNERS
annotationWithheld.clue: Close observers detect a woman among lots of fellows

clue.text: Girl with a little weight to declare

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A girl and a small weight come forward to make a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim something publicly is to make it known formally.

clue.text: Full of confidence are both conservative and communist under a fool

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Full of confidence are both conservative and communist under a fool' (7): ASS + RED is clear, but 'both conservative and' has no standard reading giving the U, so the parse cannot be stated honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: Full of confidence are both conservative and communist under a fool

clue.text: Religious man who appears in a miracle richly rewarded

indicators.note: appears in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A holy man is lavishly paid for performing a miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, a priest or minister.

clue.text: These French include true food

indicators.note: include says the French word goes around the word for true

parts.note: ces is French for these
real means true

explanation.surface: The French are said to take only genuine food.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereals are grain crops and breakfast foods.

clue.text: People who fall for advertising, the religious activity of our age

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
Mass is a religious service

explanation.surface: Consumers swallow advertisements as devoutly as a congregation, the faith of modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: Admass is a 1950s coinage for the public that mass advertising works on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the gullible mass public at whom advertising and media are aimed.

clue.text: An illegal order in the end vandals tried strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the preceding words are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Vandals ended up trying something unusual, against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the highwayman's demand to coach travellers: stop and hand over your valuables.
explanation.definitionFit: Highway robbers shouted this command to halt a coach and surrender valuables, an unlawful demand.

clue.text: Jelly included in what was pictured above the recipe

indicators.note: included in says the answer is a run of letters inside the next words

explanation.surface: A recipe book shows a photo of the finished dish above the method.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock.

clue.text: Communist leader who makes liberal muses arise

indicators.note: arise in a down clue means reading the word upwards

parts.note: there were nine Muses in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A revolutionary inspires the creative spirits of a liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Bolshevik revolution and founded the Soviet state.

clue.text: Being full, almost drive off without a kind of service

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shortened word wraps round the next piece
almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to repel is to drive off
in tennis a let is a serve that must be replayed

explanation.surface: Having eaten enough, one nearly drives off without being served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter, giving REPE; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so that wraps the tennis term.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone replete is well filled, especially with food: being full.

clue.text: Forgetting men set free in a place

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the place name

parts.note: Asia is a place, a continent

indicators.note: set free suggests the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Men are released somewhere unspecified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set free' shuffles the three letters, giving MNE; 'in' places them after the first letter of the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the condition of forgetting.

clue.text: Times when someone vulgar is surrounded by backward children

indicators.note: is surrounded by puts the vulgar person inside the reversed word
backward means the word for children is read from end to start

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring
a cad is an ill-bred, ungentlemanly man

explanation.surface: A boor finds himself among slow-learning children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like describing slow children, but it turns SEED into DEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Decades are ten-year periods, spans of time.

clue.text: Entertainers who are scorchers

explanation.definitionFit: Vocalists entertain, and anything that singes may jokingly be called by the same word.
